# Introduction

The purpose of this document is to transition the Essette application from the Service Development team to the Service Operations and Maintenance team. The runbook includes all procedures and processes used by the Maintenance and Operations staff to ensure integrity and continued operations of the application.

## Overview

The Essette application is a web-based software used by healthcare payers for care/case management activities that support the quality of health and life of the beneficiaries. The Gainwell Care Management software is designed to run on Windows servers, utilizing Microsoft Internet Information Services (IIS), Microsoft .NET Framework, and Microsoft SQL Server. It operates in a virtualized environment running VMware.

The application is a standardized Commercial Off-the-Shelf (COTS) product in which all clients are on a single web and database code. The application is highly configurable by non-technical users that have received specialized configuration training. There are no client specific customizations developed in the code stream. Releases may also contain “bug” fixes if an error has been encountered.

Dental Business Operations (DBO) is maintained within its own non-Production and Production servers and database hosted on Amazon Web Services (AWS), so there is no cross-population of Protected Health Information/Personally Identifiable Information (PHI/PII) data across clients. The AWS environment and its services are HITRUST, ISO 27001, and Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FEDRAMP) compliant. The services are also Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) compliant.

### Dental BusOps Operations Team Responsibilities

The Dental Business Operations Service Delivery Team is responsible for the following:

* Maintaining a Product Owner as a single point of contact for providing ongoing change management oversight.
  + The Product owner is Patrick Vail, Email: patrick.vail@gainwelltechnologies.com, Phone: (303) 500-6942
* Responsible for any ServiceNow ticketing requirements within the DHCS Instance of ServiceNow.
  + Create, modify, and remove users in Essette.
* Responsible for opening tickets and service requests to engage the ICC Product Engineering team in the MMIS Instance of ServiceNow.
* Assume responsibility for network connectivity at remote or host sites.
* Responsible for maintaining approved users on Essette.
  + Review and provide logs upon request.
* Dental BusOps to provide business continuity plans.
* Making available to the Gainwell Essette Leveraged team the appropriate business l resources to ensure responses and/or resolutions to issues and concerns are achieved.
  + The Essette Leverage team can communicate with the Care Management and or Member Services on a determined basis to review any topics of concern and capture any user stories to send over to the Essette Product Team to review for future releases.
  + The Essette Leverage team can communicate with the Quality Management and Quality Improvement team to explore areas to improve and streamline the process and eliminate any identified waste in Essette and in the business process.
  + The Essette Leverage team can participate in any workgroup meetings with DBO and DHCS.
* Providing Gainwell Essette Leveraged team access to all systems, information, and documentation to perform Services.
* Communicating to the Gainwell Essette Leveraged team on a timely and regular basis the business activity that would impact CD-MMIS to ensure the team can adequately prepare for any required changes. During post Go Live period, DBO will engage with the Essette Leveraged Teams mentioned above with the DBO Service Delivery team and Department of Healthcare Services (DHCS) to discuss the current state of Essette, any potential issues and a roadmap to solutions. When there is a plan to release future versions of Essette, the mentioned entities will engage in meetings to discuss the strategy of releasing the new version of Essette to the lower environments got testing then to release to production. The frequency of the meetings can be determined on the status if Essette and the needs of the mentioned entities.

## Incident and Problem Management

The Essette Maintenance & Operations team will follow the P121 - PLAN - Incident and Problem Management Plan section 4 Incident Management.

An Incident is an unplanned interruption to an IT service or reduction in the quality of an IT service. Failure of a CI that has not yet impacted service is also an Incident – for example, failure of one disk from a mirror set. The goal of the Incident Management process is to restore service as quickly as possible, whether by addressing the root cause of the Incident or implementing a workaround until the root cause can be addressed via the Problem Management process.

The objective of Incident Management is to minimize the impact of Incidents that affect the IT services. This includes:

• Ensuring that standardized methods and procedures are used for efficient and prompt response, analysis, documentation, ongoing management, and reporting of incidents.

• Increasing visibility and communication of incidents to business and IT support staff.

• Enhancing the business perception of IT through the use of a professional approach in quickly resolving and communicating incidents when they occur.

• Aligning Incident Management activities and priorities with system criticality.

• Maintaining user satisfaction with the quality of IT service.

In addition, DBO will assist with the triage of Incidents occurring in FI-supported systems that affect DBO functions.

### Communication During Incident Management

The following is the method of communication based on priority level for an incident:

• A conference bridge is opened for Priority 1 (P1) and Priority 2 (P2) incidents and Incident Coordination overseen by the Gainwell Network Operations Center (NOC) Team.

• For all P1 incidents, the NOC sends an MIM (Major Incident Management) communication to keep Management up to date. For P2 incidents with immediate risk of P1 impact a MIM is sent, if impact changes to P1 so does the priority level of the MIM.

• For P3 or lower, the communication process is handled directly between account and technician assigned to the incident ticket. The NOC Team is not engaged unless there is high and immediate risk of P1/2.

• Please refer to the DBO P121 - PLAN - Incident and Problem Management Plan

• SNOW DBO Requester User Guide

For additional information on Service-Level Determination, Adjusting Priority Levels, For Priority Levels, please refer to the DBO P121 - PLAN - Incident and Problem Management Plan

The Essette Maintenance & Operations team will follow the P121 - PLAN - Incident and Problem Management Plan section 4.9 Major Incident Management.

A Major Incident is defined as a highest-impact, highest-urgency Incident (i.e., Priority 1, Priority 2) that affects a large number of users, depriving the business of one or more operational or mission-essential capabilities.

Dental BusOps follows the above process, which opens a ticket in the Gainwell MMIS Instance of ServiceNow for the ICC Product Engineering Team. For a P1 / P2 ticket, the Operations team receives MIM (Major Incident Management) notifications from the Gainwell NOC.

Network Operations Center (NOC)

• Responds to requests for information regarding incidents in a timely manner.

• Actively monitors SolarWinds and other tools for alerts against Configuration Items (CI) 24/7, 365 days per year, excluding scheduled downtime.

• Provides assistance in quickly identifying, categorizing, and prioritizing incidents impacting infrastructure.

• Works with Incident Manager and IDL to restore service as soon as possible.

• Participates in RCA as needed.

### Customer Relationship Management Inbound Data Transfer

For inbound external files containing provider, member, and member eligibility data, the source of truth data is the California Dental-Medicaid Management Information System (CD-MMIS) Mainframe. After the data is loaded into the Dental Business Office Extract Transform and Load Master Data Hub (DBO ETL MDH), the process is initiated to create the files required by Essette.

For inbound internal files from Customer Relationship Management (CRM), member and case data are sent from CRM (the source system) to Essette (the target system) whenever specific category/area options are selected that identify an Essette care management case.

Both CRM & Essette use Application Programming Interface (API) to send and receive data, These API on the Essette side do have an expiration date approximately every 90 days both API passwords would have to be reset for CRM and Essette. If these passwords are not reset, the cases created in CRM will not be sent to Essette and would have to be manually performed.

Essette SIT and UAT, the passwords reset can be tested by the CRM and Essette teams to ensure that the change has applied successfully prior to making changes to the production environments. In the production environments this can be performed after hours, and the new password will be used for all three environments. For these passwords to be successfully updated, both the Essette and CRM M&O teams must work together to update at the same time and validate that cases can flow from CRM to Essette. A bridge line can be set up for the teams to coordinate the efforts. A bridge line will be set up for the team to work together in updating the configurations. The Essette maintenance & operations team will set reminders to update the password before the expiration date. Below are the steps that the team will take to complete the work.

1. Essette Resets password
2. Essette recycles IIS app pools
3. CRM changes APIM password
4. CRM changes environment variable
5. CRM updates custom connector
6. CRM turns off/on Essette Case Member cloud flow
7. CRM turns off/on Essette Case Note cloud flow.
8. Verify that CRM Cases can be sent to Essette.

Refer to *SDP\_Essette\_Appendix\_I\_Components\_Interface.docx* for detailed information on data transfer and interfaces.

### Application Administrator Tasks

The Amazon Web Services (AWS) Administrator verifies that that application is up and running. This Administrator is not responsible for overseeing the application’s physical infrastructure or database. Items including but not limited to the following are not the responsibility of the application Administrator: checking the capacity of the database, upgrading, or modifying the operating system and checking available disk space on servers. The AWS Administrator will have access to a console to see if the Essette Server is running, they can also shut down and start up Essette. Additional tasks that the AWS administrator may do are assist in future Essette version updates, assist in any application disaster recovery, assist in performance testing of Essette and or the AWS environment and provide results and manage AWS users to have access to the AWS systems.

Reference: P089 PLAN - Disaster Recovery Plan

### Maintenance & Operation (M&O) Duties

The amount of time the Maintenance & Operation (M&O) team spends on the tasks below depends on the volume of campaigns, modifications, and other flexible factors.

1. Maintain “front end” configurations in all Essette environments.
2. Document all configurations and changes in Essette.
3. Create, modify, user stories and manage defects in iTrace.
4. Report possible software defects to the Essette Product team.
5. Test and validate new releases and defects/fixes in Essette.
6. Create, modify, and remove users in Essette.
7. Review and provide audit logs upon request.
8. Provide support in creating and maintaining reports in Essette.
9. Support users for any Essette application needs (creation, understanding, duplicating, modifying):
   * Email
   * Meetings
   * Documentation

## Application Monitoring

Gainwell utilizes Splunk as a monitoring tool that logs files and analyzes data for operational intelligence. Splunk sends reports to the DBO, at a minimum, daily for review by the DBO for anomalies. If anomalies are determined, they are triaged and handled through the Gainwell Incident Response and Reporting Standard Operating Procedures.

Security audit event 4663is enabled on Windows servers and will be fed to Splunk, which will provide the name of the object being modified by each user. Other audit trails related to protected health information (PHI)/personally identifiable information (PII) files are received with a timestamp and security audit classification details.

Reference Section 6.3.1Application Monitoring of the *Service Design Package – Entity – Technical Specifications.docx* for more information

[resources/work-templates/assets/service-design-package/SDP Templates - Appendix P Runbooks/Examples/SDP_Appendix_P_Runbook_Example_Essette.md#security-monitoring]

## Security Monitoring

Vulnerabilities will be regularly scanned for and remediated in a timely manner in the information systems and hosted applications. Security vulnerability alerts and information will be monitored, analyzed, and distributed to personnel responsible for acting on this information in a timely manner. Known or suspected security vulnerabilities will be reported to the appropriate Threat and Vulnerability Management team. Vulnerability scans will be conducted no less frequently than monthly.

Vulnerability scanning will be performed on each system once the total system build and configuration are complete and before the system is implemented for its intended purpose as a part of the infrastructure. Compliance scans will be performed on information system components to which privileged access is authorized.

Scans will also be performed whenever a potential intrusion is identified. Scan scope will be based on previous test results, value, and sensitivity of assets and/or changes to the environment. Vulnerability scanning software will be updated before the next scheduled scan after a vulnerability becomes public.

For more information about Security Monitoring for DBO IT Services Essette see the Privacy and Security Manual, Section 16 System and Services Acquisition (SA).

[resources/work-templates/assets/service-design-package/SDP Templates - Appendix P Runbooks/Examples/SDP_Appendix_P_Runbook_Example_Essette.md#system-startup]

## System Startup

Essette is automatically started whenever the Amazon Web Services (AWS) servers are restarted. There is no need for manual or human intervention. Moreover, the Essette application is not monitored 24/7; it will be monitored only during business hours (7:00 am to 6:00 pm PST) by SiteScope for up time. The AWS administrator will be alerted in the event application services fail, which triggers alerts from site scope monitoring. The AWS Administrator will diagnose and resolve the problem to bring the Essette back online. The AWS Administrator can contact the Maintenance & Operations team to validate that Essette is online and available by logging into Essette.

For information regarding the details of the Administrator diagnosing, resolving, and bringing Essette back online, Reference: T094.8 TRP - Technology Recovery Plan - Essette.docx

Reference: P089 PLAN - Disaster Recovery
page_texts.42:
[resources/work-templates/assets/service-design-package/SDP Templates - Appendix P Runbooks/Examples/SDP_Appendix_P_Runbook_Example_Essette.md#system-shutdown]

## System Shutdown

If Essette needs to be shut down for any reason such as application version upgrade, including maintenance, this can be achieved by either shutting down the IIS Web Server or the Operating System. The type of shutdown needed depends on the type of maintenance needed. If DBO determines that there is a need to shutdown Essette, DBO coordinates with the Essette technical support team.

The DBO team would open a ticket to set up the time to shut down Essette. This would be outside of business hours The Network Operations Center (NOC), or the system administrator will shut down Essette as needed to perform an application update or release. If necessary, a bridge line would be created to work on the shutdown and any process needed to perform.

Reference: P089 PLAN - Disaster Recovery Plan.
